text: University Grants Commission Fee Refund Policy and Regulations. Higher education institutions shall refund the full fee upon withdrawal within 15 days of formal closure of admissions with a maximum deduction of Rs. 1000 processing fee. For withdrawals made up to 30 days, 80% is refunded. After 30 days, no tuition fee refund is applicable.

text:
1 | P a g e
University Grants Commission
Notification
on
December, 2016
Remittance and Refund of Fees and Other Student-centric
Issues
1. Introduction:
One of the fundamentals of the Indian higher education system, even after the
significant evolution of private sector in the domain, has remained its
commitment to provide education without profit. The rationale behind this
policy paradigm has been to protect the rights and entitlements of students
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
policy paradigm has been to protect the rights and entitlements of students
whose financial conditions often pose a roadblock to their desire for quality
higher education. For a country like India, it is but natural to promote “not-for-
profit” paradigm in view of low per capita income and high poverty index. It has
to be acknowledged that this apparently idealistic principle has worked to an
appreciable extent in India. However, the considerable number of complaints,
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
appreciable extent in India. However, the considerable number of complaints,
grievances, court cases and other references received by UGC on various
coercive and shady dealings carried out by HEIs reflect that profiteering
motivations still drive the operation of quite a few institutions in India. The
reason behind the proliferation of such malpractices can be many, including
absence of an effective and robust policy regime. However, what is most
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
absence of an effective and robust policy regime. However, what is most
disturbing about the dismal scenario is that students are at the receiving end of
this malaise. The Commission has earlier notified University Grants
Commission (Grievance Redressal) Regulations, 2012 on redressal of
multifarious grievances of students. But given the sheer volume of the
complaints regarding non-refund of fees and retention of original certificates by
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
2 | P a g e
HEIs and other related issues, the Commission has felt the need to notify
elaborate instructions so as to curb such malpractices. Considering the
seriousness of the issue, the UGC has decided to issue appropriate instructions
in the form of this notification to all universities and other higher educational
institutions under the purview of UGC.
2. Objective:
To prohibit coercive and profiteering institutional practices in the matters
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
To prohibit coercive and profiteering institutional practices in the matters
related to verification of certificates and testimonials at the time of admission,
remittance of fees and refund thereof in case of cancellation of admission and
other such student-centric issues.
In exercise of powers conferred by Section 12 (d) read with Section 12(j) of the
UGC Act, 1956, the UGC issues this notification for adoption of standard
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
UGC Act, 1956, the UGC issues this notification for adoption of standard
operating procedures in the matters related to verification of certificates and
testimonials at the time of admission, remittance of fees and refund thereof in
case of cancellation of admission and other such student-centric issues with an
aim to curb coercive and profiteering institutional practices that directly and
indirectly constrain the fundamental rights of students to explore multiple
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
indirectly constrain the fundamental rights of students to explore multiple
opportunities and choices in terms of their academic career.
3. Application and Enforcement
1.1. The instructions contained in this notification shall be in supersession to its
earlier Public Notice dated 23.04.2007. It shall be applicable to Undergraduate,
Postgraduate and Research Programs run by all statutory universities
recognized by UGC under Section 2 (f) of UGC Act, together with all colleges
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
recognized by UGC under Section 2 (f) of UGC Act, together with all colleges
under their affiliating domain and institutions declared as deemed to be
universities under Section 3 of the UGC Act.
1.2 The instructions contained in this notification shall come into force with
immediate effect and shall have regulatory force on extant as well as future
grievances over issues and matters covered herein.
1.3 Universities shall amend their relevant statutes, rules, regulations etc. and
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text: bring them in line with the provisions contained herein.
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
3 | P a g e
4. Specific Instructions and Mandatory Actions for HEIs:
The Commission herewith lays down specific instructions and consequent
mandatory actions on the issues related to (1) verification and non-retention of
students’ academic and personal certificates and testimonials, (2) remittance of
fees by students and refund thereof by the institution concerned in the event of
the cancellation of admission by the student and (3) an effective grievance
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
the cancellation of admission by the student and (3) an effective grievance
redressal mechanism to be installed by the affiliating university for quick and
effective resolution of grievances in this regard;
4.1.1 No institution of higher education shall insist upon a student to submit the
original academic and personal certificates and testimonials like mark-sheets,
school leaving certificates and other such documents at the time of submitting
admission form.
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
admission form.
4.1 Verification and Non-retention of Students’ Academic and Personal
testimonials
4.1.2 In line with instructions issued by Ministry of Personnel, Public
Grievances & Pension, Department of Administrative Reforms, PG & Pension,
the Commission has already written to HEIs about allowing self-attestation of
documents such as mark-sheets, birth certificate etc. by the applicant where
there is a system of verification of the original certificates and testimonials at
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
any stage before the finalization of the process of admission.
4.1.3 HEIs shall physically verify the originals at the time of admission of the
student in his/her presence and return them immediately after satisfying
themselves about their authenticity and veracity, keeping the attested copies for
their record.
4.1.4 The self-attested testimonials of students shall be held valid and authentic
by institution concerned and/or the affiliating university for all purposes and
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
by institution concerned and/or the affiliating university for all purposes and
administrative requirements and should there be a need for physical
verification at any time during the course of program of study, such verification
shall be undertaken in the presence of the student and certificates and
testimonials thus verified shall be returned immediately to the student.
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
4 | P a g e
4.1.5 Taking the certificates and testimonials into institutional custody under
any circumstances or pretexts is strictly prohibited for it is a coercive tactic
which can be misused for blackmailing students who wish to withdraw
admission from the institute for better prospects or other compulsions.
4.1.5 In case of any suspicion over the authenticity or genuineness of the
testimonials, the reference may be made to the university or the Board which
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
testimonials, the reference may be made to the university or the Board which
issued certificates to the student and the admission be subjected to the
authentication, but original certificates shall not be retained under any
circumstances
4.2.1 No HEI shall make it mandatory for applicants to purchase the
institutional prospectus any time during the course of the program of study.
Purchasing prospectus shall be the personal choice of the student and he/she
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
Purchasing prospectus shall be the personal choice of the student and he/she
has all rights to decide against it in case he/she wishes to access the information
from institutional website. As laid down in the Right to Information Act, 2005,
and reiterated in the UGC Guidelines on Students’ Entitlement, all HEIs shall
disclose on their website and prospectus information like the status of the
institution, its affiliation, accreditation rating, physical assets and amenities,
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
course-wise sanctioned intake of students, details of faculty, membership of
governing bodies and minutes of the meetings of bodies like
Academic/Executive council, sources of income and the financial situation and
any other information about its functioning necessary for a student to make a
fully informed choice.
4.2 Remittance and Refund of Fees
4.2.2 HEIs shall charge fees in advance only for the semester/year in which a
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
4.2.2 HEIs shall charge fees in advance only for the semester/year in which a
student is to engage in academic activities. Collecting advance fees for entire
program of study or for more than one semester/year in which a student is
enrolled is strictly prohibited as it restricts the student from exercising other
options of enrolment elsewhere. This enabling provision is in line with the UGC
guidelines on Choice-Based Credit System (CBCS) and Model Curricula which
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
guidelines on Choice-Based Credit System (CBCS) and Model Curricula which
are geared towards promoting a student’s inter-institutional mobility.
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
5 | P a g e
4.2.3 If a student chooses to withdraw from the program of study in which
he/she is enrolled, the institution concerned shall follow the following four-tier
system for the refund of fees remitted by the student.
Sr.
No
Percentage of Refund of
Aggregate fees*
Point of time when notice of
withdrawal of admission is
served to HEI
(1) 100% 15 days before the formally-notified
last date of admission
(2) 80% Not more than 15 days after the
formally-notified last date of
admission
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
formally-notified last date of
admission
(3) 50% More than 15 days but less than 30
days after formally-notified last date
of admission
(4) 00% More than 30 days after formally-
notified last date of admission
*(Inclusive of course fees and non-tuition fees but exclusive of caution money
and security deposit)
4.2.4 In case of (1) in the table above, the HEI concerned shall deduct an
amount not more than 10% of the aggregate fees as processing charges from the
refundable amount.
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
refundable amount.
4.2.5 Fees shall be refunded by all HEIs to an eligible student within fifteen
days from the date of receiving a written application from him/her in this
regard.
4.3.1 All universities shall mandatorily constitute a “Grievance Redressal
Committee” (GRC) mandated by UGC (Grievance Redressal) Regulations 2012
to address and effectively resolve complaints, representations and grievances
related to any of the issues mentioned in this notification, among others
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
related to any of the issues mentioned in this notification, among others
articulated in the regulations. The GRC shall do all it takes to ensure that its
4.3 Constitution and Functions of Grievance Redressal Committee
(GRC)
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
6 | P a g e
departments and affiliated colleges unfailingly comply with all the instructions
articulated in this notification.
4.3.2 The GRC shall follow procedures outlined in UGC (Grievance Redressal)
Regulations 2012 for resolution of the students’ grievances in above matters.
5. Punitive Actions by Commission against defaulting HEIs
5.1 Any act of retention of original certificate or non-refund of fee by any college
shall be deemed to have been committed by the affiliating university which
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
shall be deemed to have been committed by the affiliating university which
shall only be liable for punitive action by the UGC.
5.2 On receiving any complaint from students or aggrieved person on any of the
issues outlined in this notification, the Commission shall forward it to the GRC
of the university concerned for feedback.
5.3 The GRC of the university concerned shall furnish to Commission the
“Action Taken Report” and/or status of the grievance resolution within a period
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
“Action Taken Report” and/or status of the grievance resolution within a period
of twenty days from the date of receipt of the Commission’s missive.
5.4 On basis of the feedback of the GRC, if the Commission feels the defaulting
HEI is wilfully contravening the provisions contained in this Notification, it
shall take all such punitive actions as notified in Regulation 9 of UGC
(Grievance Redressal) Regulations 2012 against the defaulting HEIs.
title: uploads_doc_fee-refund-policy-1_pdf_bdaa8b77

text:
(Grievance Redressal) Regulations 2012 against the defaulting HEIs.
5.5 Additionally, the Commission shall write to accreditation agencies about the
misconduct and malpractices of the erring HEI with the request to take all such
actions as deemed fit by them to ensure compliance.
(Jaspal S. Sandhu)
Secretary

text:
Cloud Data Engineer Trainee – Campus Hire JD
Job Description
Cloud Data Engineer Trainee – Campus Hire
Role Title: Cloud Data Engineer Trainee – Campus Hire
Program Context: Structured college-based training program aligned to cloud data engineering, data
warehousing, SQL, Python, PySpark, multi-cloud data platforms, GenAI-enabled data solutions, and capstone-
based project readiness.
Role Summary
title: Cloud_Data_Engineer_Trainee_Detailed_JD

text:
based project readiness.
Role Summary
We are looking for high-potential campus hires from engineering institutions who will undergo a structured
Cloud Data Engineer training program. The program is designed to build strong fundamentals in data
warehousing, data modeling, SQL, Python, PySpark, cloud-native data services, data quality, governance, and
end-to-end data pipeline development.
The trainee will be trained across data warehouse architecture, dimensional modeling, ETL/ELT, SQL and
title: Cloud_Data_Engineer_Trainee_Detailed_JD

text:
procedural SQL, Python programming, data libraries, PySpark, GitHub Copilot utilization, GenAI for data
engineering, GCP Data, Azure Data, AWS Data, and an end-to-end capstone project. By the end of the program,
the trainee is expected to demonstrate the ability to design, build, validate, optimize, and present cloud-based
data engineering solutions.
Key Learning Areas
1. Data Warehousing & Architecture
title: Cloud_Data_Engineer_Trainee_Detailed_JD

text:
Key Learning Areas
1. Data Warehousing & Architecture
Build foundational understanding of data warehousing, the role of a Data Engineer versus BI Developer and
Analyst, OLTP versus OLAP systems, Data Warehouse versus Data Lake versus Lakehouse, and common data
warehousing use cases.
Learn data warehouse architecture including source, staging, warehouse and BI layers, ingestion layer, staging
layer design, Enterprise Data Warehouse, data marts, and modern architectures such as Lambda, Kappa, and
title: Cloud_Data_Engineer_Trainee_Detailed_JD

text:
Lakehouse.
2. Data Modeling, Dimensional Modeling & Warehouse Design
Gain exposure to conceptual, logical, and physical data models, ER modeling, entities, attributes, relationships,
normalization, denormalization, data cleansing, and data manipulation.
Learn dimensional modeling concepts including star schema, snowflake schema, galaxy schema, fact tables,
dimension tables, conformed dimensions, role-playing dimensions, junk dimensions, degenerate dimensions,
title: Cloud_Data_Engineer_Trainee_Detailed_JD

text:
keys, referential integrity, Slowly Changing Dimensions, grain definition, hierarchies, sparsity handling,
aggregation tables, and performance-oriented warehouse design.
title: Cloud_Data_Engineer_Trainee_Detailed_JD

text:
Cloud Data Engineer Trainee – Campus Hire JD
3. ETL/ELT, Data Quality, Metadata & Governance
Understand ETL/ELT concepts, schema-on-write versus schema-on-read, batch versus streaming, data
ingestion and processing patterns, and tools used in pipeline construction.
Apply data quality practices including profiling, cleaning, validation, standardization, lineage, DQ metrics,
handling structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data, metadata management, data catalog basics,
title: Cloud_Data_Engineer_Trainee_Detailed_JD

text:
governance principles, and data security basics.
4. SQL, NoSQL & Procedural SQL for Data Engineering
Develop strong SQL capability covering SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, DISTINCT, LIMIT, joins, aggregations,
subqueries, CTEs, window functions, CASE statements, NULL handling, JSON handling, performance
optimization, indexing concepts, execution plan basics, and partition pruning.
Learn SQL for data engineering including ETL pipeline SQL, data validation queries, reconciliation queries,
title: Cloud_Data_Engineer_Trainee_Detailed_JD

text:
incremental data processing, NoSQL fundamentals, stored procedures, functions, packages, cursors, loops,
conditional statements, exception handling, logging errors, triggers, and procedure usage in ETL pipelines.
5. Python for Data Engineering
Build Python fundamentals including syntax, variables, data types, input/output, operators, control flow,
functions, modules, scope, lists, strings, tuples, dictionaries, sets, file handling, OOP, exception handling,
title: Cloud_Data_Engineer_Trainee_Detailed_JD

text:
debugging, unit testing, logging, virtual environments, and package management.
Gain hands-on exposure to Python data libraries and utilities including NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, Datetime,
Requests, OS module, JSON processing, API calls, basic web scraping, SQLite basics, regular expressions,
iterators, generators, decorators, and functional programming concepts.
6. PySpark, Spark SQL & Big Data Processing
title: Cloud_Data_Engineer_Trainee_Detailed_JD

text:
6. PySpark, Spark SQL & Big Data Processing
Learn PySpark fundamentals including Spark architecture, driver, executor, cluster manager, setup, Spark UI
basics, RDD operations, DataFrames, transformations, joins, aggregations, Spark SQL, views, window
functions, and file handling with CSV, JSON, Parquet, and data lake integration.
7. GitHub Copilot & GenAI for Data Engineering
Develop awareness of GitHub Copilot basics, Copilot suggestions, Copilot in IDEs, language support,
title: Cloud_Data_Engineer_Trainee_Detailed_JD

text:
generative commit messages, Copilot Chat, Copilot for CLI, code documentation, optimization, refactoring,
debugging, NLP with Copilot, limitations, troubleshooting, and usage in existing or legacy code.
Gain exposure to GenAI fundamentals, NLP basics, prompt engineering, working with LLM APIs using Python,
GenAI for SQL query generation, data query automation, data summarization, insight generation, RAG for data
systems, and GenAI with Pandas and DataFrames.
title: Cloud_Data_Engineer_Trainee_Detailed_JD

text:
systems, and GenAI with Pandas and DataFrames.
Candidate to learn any 1 of the following 3 platforms as part of the training.
8. GCP Data Engineering
Learn GCP fundamentals including hierarchy and resource management, regions and zones, IAM, Cloud
Console, Cloud Shell, monitoring, logging, error reporting, virtual machines, SSH access, preemptible VMs, and
service account security.
title: Cloud_Data_Engineer_Trainee_Detailed_JD

text:
Cloud Data Engineer Trainee – Campus Hire JD
Develop exposure to GCP data services including Cloud Storage, Dataflow with Apache Beam for batch and
streaming pipelines, BigQuery, Dataproc, Cloud Composer, managed Airflow, pipeline deployment, scheduling,
monitoring, partitioning, clustering, external tables, materialized views, and security management.
9. Azure Data Engineering
Learn Azure fundamentals including resource groups, subscriptions, regions, Azure AD, RBAC, Azure Portal,
title: Cloud_Data_Engineer_Trainee_Detailed_JD

text:
Azure CLI, Azure Monitor, Log Analytics, virtual machines, SSH access, and managed identities.
Build exposure to ADLS Gen2, Azure Data Factory, Azure Databricks, Databricks Lakehouse architecture,
notebooks, clusters, workflows, Unity Catalog basics, Spark, Delta Lake, data ingestion, Lakeflow, data
validation, data quality checks, logging, monitoring, alerting, SLA management, and Azure OpenAI integration
with data pipelines.
10. AWS Data Engineering
title: Cloud_Data_Engineer_Trainee_Detailed_JD

text:
with data pipelines.
10. AWS Data Engineering
Learn AWS fundamentals including account structure, regions, availability zones, IAM, roles and policies, AWS
Console and CLI, CloudWatch, CloudTrail, error monitoring, EC2, and SSH access.
Gain exposure to Amazon S3, Redshift, AWS Glue, Glue Studio, data lake architecture, Kinesis, Lambda, Step
Functions, EMR, Athena, Lake Formation, DMS, API Gateway, CI/CD basics, CloudFormation/Terraform
title: Cloud_Data_Engineer_Trainee_Detailed_JD

text:
introduction, deployment of data pipelines, Amazon Bedrock, LLM integration, and AI-powered data pipelines.
11. Capstone Project Readiness
Apply learned concepts through an end-to-end capstone project involving file/API ingestion, transformation,
storage, SQL analytics, and one GenAI use case.
Key Responsibilities During Training
• Participate actively in the structured Cloud Data Engineer training program delivered in college.
title: Cloud_Data_Engineer_Trainee_Detailed_JD

text:
• Build foundational understanding of data warehousing, data architecture, dimensional modeling, ETL/ELT,
data quality, metadata, lineage, governance, and security basics.
• Design data models, fact-dimension relationships, SCD handling, keys, relationships, warehouse
optimization patterns, and performance-aware data structures.
• Write SQL for analytics, transformations, data validation, reconciliation, incremental processing, semi-
structured data handling, and ETL automation.
title: Cloud_Data_Engineer_Trainee_Detailed_JD

text:
structured data handling, and ETL automation.
• Develop Python scripts for data processing, file handling, JSON processing, API calls, data manipulation
using Pandas and NumPy, testing, logging, and debugging.
• Build PySpark-based data processing logic using RDDs, DataFrames, Spark SQL, joins, aggregations,
window functions, and file formats such as CSV, JSON, and Parquet.
• Use GitHub Copilot responsibly for documentation, code optimization, refactoring, debugging, SQL
title: Cloud_Data_Engineer_Trainee_Detailed_JD

text:
generation, and productivity enhancement while validating output quality and correctness.
• Gain hands-on exposure to cloud data engineering services across GCP, Azure, and AWS.
• Build, monitor, validate, and present cloud-based data pipelines using batch, streaming, orchestration,
data lake, warehouse, governance, and GenAI concepts.
• Complete assessments and the final end-to-end capstone project with demo, code walkthrough, Q&A, and
peer review.

facts, dimensions, keys, SCDs, hierarchies, and aggregation tables.
